The lock branch returns the base import-only message or drops the explicit exhausted-wait wording.
Either exception branch omits the instruction to promote again.
The lock branch retains the import script, including when the old handler is restored.
A store failure is swallowed or raised as a different exception type.
Exception chaining is removed or its SQLite cause is replaced.
A row is written despite refusal while the real write lock is held.
The post-release append fails or reports a result other than written.
The successful retry fails to persist the expected literal run identity.
Non-contention failures lose the import repair or its independently specified project argument.
Non-contention failures are misclassified as exhausted locks.
The wrapper loses or replaces the injected exception as its cause; the injected object and observed exception chain do not move together automatically.
